citations.narrative:
Several areas of the facility needed repair and maintenance. All structures must be maintained in good repair to help
protect the enclosed animals.
-A section of broken wire panel was lying on the ground near the first water crossing. Animals may become injured from
entrapment in the discarded panel section.
-Near the entrance to the camel enclosure, a section of wire fence paneling was damaged. A large hole in the fence,
approximately 4 feet x 4 feet, had varying length of wires with sharp points extending into the enclosure.
-A length of older fencing just prior to the camel enclosure was damaged with loose wires and multiple holes which could
be a source of entrapment to the animals. A metal t post had been left leaning inside the enclosure and could be a source
of injury to the animals.
-The enclosure housing thirteen Jacob sheep had a piece of damaged tin on the door of the shelter entry that had several
sharp edges. Near the shelter structure lumber material on the ground had an exposed screw that could cause injury to
the animals. A tree had fallen inside the enclosure that had fencing material wrapped around the tree trunk. The wire
fencing material was broken and had numerous sharp points. Animals could be injured from the sharp points in the
enclosure or become entangled in the old fencing.
_The enclosure for the white tiger had numerous pieces of tin wrapped around several trees that had large holes and
numerous sharp edges. The sharp edges could cause injury to the tiger.
-Near the giraffe enclosure, the wire portion of the metal pipe enclosure fence for the male watusi had been damaged and
needed repairs to prevent potential injury to animals.
-The enclosure housing three nilgai had several sections of the enclosure fence that was damaged near the ground. The
damaged fencing had several sharp points extending into the enclosure, and portions of the broken wire that could cause
entrapment to the animals.
All structures must be maintained in good repair to help protect the enclosed animals. The indoor and outdoor housing
facilities shall be structurally sound and shall be maintained in good repair to protect the animals from injury and to
contain the animals.
To be corrected by 6-29-2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
Additional Inspectors:
Michael Tygart, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
